**Finding submitted: deviation on § 3.4 (p0022), redlined to the fallback position.**

**What I found**
- § 3.4 is the only audit/inspection right running against us: HDI's General Manager may inspect the records of our General Manager relating to the Net Sales payment calculation. I confirmed there is no other verification, access or books-and-records right anywhere (§ 1.4 access rights run *in our favour*; §§ 5.4, 8 and 10 contain none).
- Notice: 30 days' prior written notice — meets the **preferred** standard.
- Timing: during our normal business hours — meets preferred.
- Cost: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI" — unconditional, better than either the 5 % or 10 % underpayment carve-out.
- Scope: records only, no system or remote access — nothing to delete.
- **Frequency: unlimited.** That is expressly walk-away territory, so the clause fails the fallback on a material term.

**The change (one surgical replace, minimality gate passed)**
> "may**, no more than once per year and** upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect..."

That single insertion is all that is needed to land the clause on the fallback, since notice and cost are already met (mapped as `already_met` with verbatim quotes).

**Noted, not flagged:** the inspection is by HDI's own General Manager rather than an independent, confidentiality-bound auditor, and there is no off-site-where-possible wording. These are preferred-level refinements only, and HDI is separately bound by the § 8.3 confidentiality covenant, so I have not pressed them.
